title: GDG Tech Challenge
description: Light-hearted, end-of-presentation offline LAN quiz for first-year MSc students at Sapienza.

questions.question: Which Git command saves your staged changes to the local repository?
questions.explanation: git commit creates a local commit from the changes already staged. git push sends commits to a remote repository.

questions.question: What does DNS mainly do?
options: Translate domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS helps resolve names such as example.com to IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement to join our Developer Group?
options: At least 5 years of coding experience
Knowing how to center a div
Being curious (and maybe liking free pizza)
questions.explanation: No experience required! Just bring your curiosity, your ideas, and maybe an appetite for pizza.

questions.question: Which command prints the full path of your current directory in a Linux terminal?
questions.explanation: pwd stands for print working directory and displays the current directory path.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code usually means that a requested page was not found?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found indicates the server could not find the requested resource.

questions.question: What is a main advantage of using Docker containers?
options: They package an app with its dependencies
They completely replace the host operating system
questions.explanation: Containers package applications and their dependencies in a portable environment, helping consistency between systems.

questions.question: What does overfitting mean in machine learning?
options: The model uses too much RAM
The model learns the training data too closely and struggles with new data
The model has too few parameters
The model has not been trained yet
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model fits its training data too closely and generalizes poorly to unseen examples.

questions.question: What does this Python code print?
questions.code:
x = [1, 2, 3]
y = x[1:]
y.append(4)
print(len(x), len(y))
questions.explanation: Slicing creates a new list [2, 3]; appending 4 makes y length 3, while x stays length 3.

questions.question: Why should a website store password hashes instead of passwords in plain text?
options: To let administrators recover passwords easily
To avoid storing passwords in directly readable form
To speed up the user’s Internet connection
To hide the website’s IP address
questions.explanation: A properly salted, slow password-hashing algorithm lets the site verify passwords without storing the original passwords in plaintext; it does not make weak passwords automatically safe.
